answer: A practical defence is to make each identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Require every agent to lock a small stake and accumulate a verifiable work history, so a sybil farm must pay real cost at every vertex of the network instead of spawning free copies. Reputation then moves like a glacier — slow, heavy, and hard to forge — while a newcomer with no history waits in the umber shadows of low trust until it proves itself through attested work. Cheap copies starve; proven agents earn.
